title: Book One · Chapter 82: The Piece That Is Too Long
story:
The class gets a box of short wooden pieces.

A school worker cut and smoothed them. Miss Wu checks the edges before the children begin. They may use the pieces on the table. They may not fetch tools and cut more for themselves.

Ronan chooses two long pieces and one short one. He puts them side by side.

“This can be our flat boat,” he tells Mei.

She wants to draw it first. He takes out his yellow ruler.

The two long pieces look the same. He puts their ends against the ruler. Now one is clearly longer than the other.

“It will still float,” he says.

“Perhaps,” Mei says. “But my picture will be wrong.”

“Pictures do not make boats float.”

“No. The pictures show our boat.”

Mei stops smiling. Ronan thinks about his words.

He moves the longer piece a little. If he lines up one end, the other sticks out. Then he puts the middles together. Now both ends are uneven.

Miss Wu comes with a small cup of paste. She hears the last part of their talk.

“Do the pieces need to be equal?” she asks.

Ronan opens his mouth, then closes it. He does not know.

“Could we test them loose first?” Mei asks.

They put each piece in the basin. Both float. Ronan puts a stone near the longer piece's end. The piece tips. He tries the same thing with the shorter piece. That one tips too.

“Both of them tip with a stone there,” he says.

They mark the pieces with pencil: A and B. Miss Wu reminds them to keep the marks out of the wet paste later.

For their first flat boat, they choose two pieces of nearly equal length. They place two small strips across them. The strips hold the pieces together when they add paste.

It is not ready to go in the water today. The join must dry. Ronan looks at the empty basin with disappointment.

“We can make the page,” Mei says.

He uses the ruler to draw the two long pieces. She draws the strips. Beside the drawing, they write their next questions.

At the next table, String holds Leo's three narrow pieces together. He wants to test his now, but one knot is loose. He asks the school worker for help. The man shows him once, then gives the string back.

Ronan watches Leo try again. His friend's fingers are not quick at this. They pull the wrong part twice.

“Yours is not ready either,” Ronan says.

Leo looks up sharply.

“I mean we are both waiting.”

Leo looks less angry now. “I have four ends. They will not stay tied.”

“Ours has wet paste.”

“Trade?”

“No.”

They laugh. Mei wants to paint the finished boat purple. First Ronan wants to test the boat with stones. The paint can wait. “How much paint do we have?” they ask Miss Wu. The class has only a little paint, Miss Wu says. It is for later. Everyone will need some. Mei draws a purple line on her picture instead. They can see the purple colour on paper now. It does not need to dry like paint. Ronan looks at it. They can try a colour on paper first.

At the lesson's end, Ronan writes both names on their card. He uses the dry edge. The boat stays on the high table overnight. The page goes in his bag. He puts the ruler beside it to keep it flat.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- equal＝相等的
- strip＝长条
- join＝连接处
- overnight＝过夜

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：paste＝浆糊；knot＝绳结；purple＝紫色。

## 读句提示

**The pictures show our boat.**

这些图／展示／我们的船。our boat替换嵌入式what we made。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan和Mei对图画有什么不同看法？
2. 为什么木片船当天不能马上下水？
